span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Persona settings act as a proxy that embeds social preferences and bounded rationality into the agents; without them the agents' improved reasoning drives them to the subgame-perfect solution instead of to human-like fairness behaviour
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Randomly generated persona attributes in earlier studies injected noise into agent behaviour, which masked the effect of reasoning ability and prevented it from being evaluated systematically
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: Skew in how the agents' offers were distributed across offer values drives the fitted acceptance-rate lines to impossible values above 1.0 or below 0, producing the anomalies seen in the responder-side figures
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Excluding persona settings in order to isolate reasoning ability is itself a limitation, since personas are known to shape human-like behaviour.
span.note: what this limits: the transfer to agents with personas: WHILE OUR METHODOLOGICAL CHOICE CLARIFIES THE ROLE OF REASONING ABILITY, IT ALSO REPRESENTS A LIMITATION OF THIS STUDY - the excluded factor is known to matter
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The sample size of 1000 decisions per condition was chosen pragmatically rather than by a formal power analysis.
span.note: what this limits: the precision of every estimate: WHILE THIS NUMBER IS NOT DERIVED FROM A FORMAL POWER ANALYSIS, IT WAS SELECTED BASED ON TWO MAIN CONSIDERATIONS
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Scope is restricted to decision-making and negotiation tasks; market-level and institutional applications are left to future work.
span.note: what this limits: the scope of the conclusions: BROADER APPLICATIONS TO MARKET-LEVEL MODELING OR INSTITUTIONAL DESIGN REMAIN IMPORTANT DIRECTIONS FOR FUTURE WORK
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Earlier claims of success are attributed to the coarseness of the evaluation rather than to the agents: aggregate distributions and binary alignment, with no individual-level analysis.
span.note: what this limits: published findings that generative agents reproduce human behaviour in economic games: this paper states those successes may stem from coarse-grained criteria — aggregate distributions or binary alignment — without individual-level or reasoning-process analysis
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The expectation the title asks about is not borne out: greater reasoning ability does not directly produce reproduction of the experiments.
span.note: what this limits: the assumption that a more capable model will simulate an economic experiment better: this paper reports zero-shot prompting with an older model aligning closely with human behaviour, and states improving reasoning ability cannot lead directly to reproduction
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The paper's own explanation of why earlier work succeeded is a claim about MEASUREMENT RESOLUTION, not about behaviour: prior studies assessed aggregate distributions or binary alignment 'without deeper analysis of underlying reasoning processes or individual-level deviations'. On that account the earlier results are not wrong, they are coarse - which is a harder thing to test.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Agent outputs are reported as highly sensitive to design choices - persona, prompt formulation, role instructions - so any single configuration's result is conditional on choices the paper had to make and could not vary at once.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Prompt-engineering techniques for eliciting language-model reasoning are imported into the agent-based-modelling tradition of experimental economics, with prompts standing in for experimental instructions to human subjects.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: the in-context examples RE-DRAWN AT RANDOM from the raw data and the whole simulation re-run several times, alongside runs at 15 and 20 examples
span.note: eliminates: the particular examples chosen for the prompt as the source of the result - an LLM's behaviour is conditioned on its examples, so a finding from one draw is a fact about that draw
Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Raising the reasoning ability of LLM-driven agents pushed their ultimatum-game behaviour toward the game-theoretic solution and away from the real human experimental data.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: No prompting condition produced a distribution that statistically matched either the theoretical solution or the human experimental data.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: On the proposer side the older, weaker-reasoning model with zero-shot prompting was also relatively close to human behaviour, showing that better reasoning does not straightforwardly buy better reproduction of economic experiments.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: On the responder side, chain-of-thought prompting produced the closest match to the theoretical (rational) distribution of any condition.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Against human responder data the ranking inverted: the weakest-reasoning condition, zero-shot gpt-3.5, matched human acceptance behaviour most closely.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: The authors conclude that LLM agents do not spontaneously behave like humans in economic games without prompts carrying social context, so using LLM-driven multi-agent simulations as substitutes for real human groups is currently unwarranted.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.

span.label: Zero-shot prompting with gpt-4 collapsed the proposer distribution: at every temperature almost every agent proposed an even 50–50 split, eliminating the spread of offers seen in real experiments.
span.note: Quotation withheld because this record is not cleared for redistribution.
